summary: Join this course on Sexual and Gender-Based Violence in Humanitarian Settings. Gain essential knowledge and skills to address and prevent violence effectively.
lede: Sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) training for humanitarian settings helps response teams assess risks and plan safe, survivor-centred services. For GBV officers, protection specialists, safeguarding leads and humanitarian managers, it covers risk assessment, referral pathway design, prevention planning, informed consent, confidentiality and responsible information management. Participants practise safety audits, service mapping, mitigation planning and accountable reporting; advanced clinical and legal procedures are introduced only at overview level.
audienceIntro: This foundation-to-intermediate course suits professionals who make or influence SGBV prevention, protection, referral, safeguarding, and accountability decisions during humanitarian response and recovery. It is designed for role holders who need practical tools without assuming advanced clinical, investigative, or data-engineering expertise.
modules: SGBV Case Management and Psychosocial Support
prerequisites: No advanced clinical, legal, investigative, or programming background is required. You should have basic experience in humanitarian, development, protection, health, safeguarding, or community-service operations and be prepared to handle sensitive scenarios respectfully. Coding is not required. Advanced data and clinical topics receive conceptual or operational treatment rather than technical engineering or clinical certification.
